etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English misser, from Late Latin miser (“wretched, unfortunate, unhappy, miserable, sick, ill, bad, worthless, etc.”).
senses: (derogatory) A person who hoards money rather than spending it; one who is cheap or extremely parsimonious. [late 16th c.]
(obsolete) A person who is wretched or despicable; a wretch.
